da--us-da001-confirmed-fundamental-scree.content:
# DA001 — Confirmed fundamental improvement, quarter-end screen

**Neither tested signal advances. The confirmed score earned a mean 1.62% a quarter over the equal-weight universe after costs, and compounded to +32.98% against +30.12% for SPY and +22.92% for the universe. It was positive in only 4 of 7 windows, and its partial rank IC was positive in only 4 of 7. Both fall short of the declared 5 of 7. This is a failed screen for the tested specification, not proof that the mechanism is absent, and it is not Alpha.**




Seven windows cannot separate an effect of this size from zero: the V0 t-like ratio is 0.74. Excess return also moved with the market, with a correlation of 0.73 for V0 and 0.91 for V1, so high-beta exposure is a likelier explanation than underreaction. The predicted home of the effect failed as well: thin names lost 2.82% a quarter against their tier after costs, while liquid names gained 4.03%.




## Results




| Measure | V0 confirmed | V1 operating income | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q+1 mean net excess over universe | +1.62% | +2.69% | above 0 |
| Windows positive | 4 of 7 | 4 of 7 | at least 5 |
| Compounded net return, SPY +30.12% | +32.98% | +42.84% | above SPY |
| Mean partial rank IC | 0.029 | 0.007 | above 0 |
| IC windows positive | 4 of 7 | 3 of 7 | at least 5 |
| Same-cohort Q+1 gross excess | +2.94% | +4.40% | above 0 |
| Average of Q+3 and Q+4 increments | +0.82% | +0.74% | below Q+1 |
| Verdict | G1 and G3 fail | G1 and G3 fail | all four |




Returns exclude dividends for stocks and SPY alike. V0's gross excess by horizon is +2.30% at Q+1 (7 cohorts), +3.46% at Q+2 (6), +0.40% at Q+3 (5) and +1.79% at Q+4 (4). G4 passes on the four complete cohorts, but Q+2 above Q+1 over all cohorts means the month-scale shape is unproven.




| Formation | Universe Q+1 | SPY | V0 net excess | V0 partial IC | V1 net excess |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2024-12-31 | -10.5% | -4.6% | -1.4% | +0.065 | -3.4% |
| 2025-03-31 | +9.9% | +10.5% | +7.3% | -0.004 | +7.4% |
| 2025-06-30 | +9.5% | +7.8% | +3.7% | -0.016 | +7.1% |
| 2025-09-30 | +0.9% | +2.4% | -0.5% | +0.045 | +3.5% |
| 2025-12-31 | -0.6% | -4.6% | -8.1% | -0.005 | -2.3% |
| 2026-03-31 | +19.2% | +14.8% | +9.0% | +0.026 | +7.8% |
| 2026-06-30 | -4.6% | +2.1% | +1.5% | +0.095 | -1.1% |




## Diagnostics




Requiring all three fundamentals to improve did not beat the operating-income baseline on return: V0 trails V1 by 1.07% a quarter, though its IC is higher. Doubled costs leave V0 at +0.94% a quarter and +26.93% compounded, below SPY. Charging -100% to basket names missing at the next snapshot leaves +0.70%, so the sign does not flip, and only 12 of 1,308 basket positions were affected.




Leaving out one window moves V0's mean between +0.40% and +3.25%. The top-20 basket shows +10.02% a quarter for V0 and +11.40% for V1, but V0 is positive in only 4 of 7 windows and its mean sits well above its median in the strong windows. Names such as SNDK, MU and SEZL carry those windows. A review of the largest winners' split factors and liquidity found no defect, so the gains stay in the record. This is a diagnostic, and treating it as the primary now would be retuning on returns.




## Method and limits




Formations are the seven quarter ends from 2024-12-31 to 2026-06-30, with 1,808 to 1,912 scored names each. Liquid nonfinancial common stocks with a recent original 10-K or 10-Q were ranked on year-over-year changes in revenue, operating income and cash flow over assets, all from one filing. V0 takes the lowest of the three ranks. The top decile was held from close to close and charged a full round trip every quarter, at 25 bp per side above $20m of formation dollar volume and 50 bp below.




Prices are quarter-end snapshots rather than modeled fills, and formation-day dollar volume is a noisy liquidity measure. The partial IC for 2024-12-31 has no prior-return control. Names missing at a later snapshot are held flat. Three names with split-like share jumps were quarantined before signals were joined; 90 of 151 flagged moves had no usable share history and stay unverified. Funded NAV and Sharpe are not applicable to seven quarterly marks. All data was already exposed, so nothing here is independent validation. External requests: 0.




## Next decision




This specification stops here, with no threshold, window or universe retuned. It is one completed no-pass Batch, and the Guess stays open. Isolating liquid names or the top 20 would be a return-driven change and must be recorded as such. The real limit is seven windows: resolving an effect near 2% a quarter needs a much longer history, which means new external data and the owner's approval.

# DA002 — Fund-filed initial Schedule 13D, quarter-end screen

**The candidate fails clearly. Buying stocks after a fund-like initial 13D lost 6.04% a quarter against matched stocks after costs, with 0 of 7 windows positive. It compounded to -22.77% while SPY made +30.12% and the control universe +20.68%. The placebo of non-fund filers lost about the same, 5.92% a quarter, so the fund-versus-other distinction the mechanism needs did not appear. This tested long specification stops here.**




The shortfall is not an artifact of the comparison. Two hundred random baskets of the same size drawn from the controls averaged +0.09% gross, with a 95% range of -3.40% to +6.04%; the candidate's -5.20% gross is at the bottom of that range. It is less severe at the median: the median name trails its cell median by 2.45% a window, with 3 of 7 positive. Part of the gap is therefore a missing right tail, as the controls include lottery-like winners that these baskets did not.




## Results




| Measure | V0 fund-like | V1 placebo | Required of V0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Q+1 mean net matched excess | -6.04% | -5.92% | above 0 |
| Windows positive | 0 of 7 | 2 of 7 | at least 5 |
| Compounded net return, SPY +30.12% | -22.77% | -15.37% | above SPY |
| Slope on control universe return | 0.18 | -0.39 | at most 0.25 |
| Same-cohort Q+1 gross excess | -6.47% | -6.19% | above 0 |
| Average of Q+3 and Q+4 increments | -3.64% | -10.15% | below Q+1 |
| Verdict | Only the slope gate passes | Not eligible | all five |




| Formation | Names | Basket Q+1 | Matched | V0 net excess | V1 net excess |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2024-12-31 | 30 | -17.9% | -9.1% | -9.8% | -3.6% |
| 2025-03-31 | 38 | +8.5% | +9.0% | -1.4% | -7.6% |
| 2025-06-30 | 33 | +3.0% | +10.0% | -7.8% | +2.6% |
| 2025-09-30 | 41 | -8.4% | +1.0% | -10.2% | -19.3% |
| 2025-12-31 | 38 | -4.0% | -1.0% | -3.9% | -4.4% |
| 2026-03-31 | 41 | +12.7% | +16.1% | -4.2% | -14.2% |
| 2026-06-30 | 19 | -9.6% | -5.4% | -5.0% | +5.2% |




## Diagnostics




Gross excess stays negative at every horizon: -5.20% at Q+1, -3.59% at Q+2, -1.23% at Q+3 and -4.22% at Q+4. There is no positive effect to decay. Thin names lose 7.18% a quarter and liquid names 2.22%. Subjects where the same filer earlier filed a 13G, the sharper signal of a passive holder turning active, show -3.95% gross, positive in 3 of 7 windows across 6 to 11 names. Filing age does not rescue it, at -4.84% within 30 days, -2.42% from 31 to 60 and -8.50% beyond 60.




Doubled costs give -6.88% a quarter. Charging -100% to the 16 of 240 positions missing at the next snapshot gives -12.72%. Holding them flat also ignores any takeover premium they earned, so that bound is one-sided. Pharma and biotech are only 10.4% of V0 against 9.4% of the universe, and removing them leaves -6.38% gross, so biotech financing is not the explanation.




The market-slope gate passed at 0.18, so the DA001 problem did not recur, but it was passing on a loss. All this inspection after the result is descriptive and changes no verdict.




## Method and limits




Formations are the DA001 quarter ends, with 3,043 to 3,227 eligible names and 19 to 41 subjects. An event is an initial 13D filed in the 92 days before formation, with a subject in the liquid universe, listed at least about 270 days and not a blank-check company. Filer type comes from name words in the EDGAR index, and no filing text was read. That label is crude: it holds activists alongside family vehicles, strategic investors and deal buyers, whose stocks may be capped at a deal price. Matching uses dollar volume, not market value, and only one prior quarter of return. It also omits industry and valuation.




Prices are quarter-end close proxies without dividends. The latest window has only 19 subjects, after recent listings and blank-check companies removed many filings. The t-like ratio of -4.85 rests on seven windows and overlapping issuers, so it should not be read as a precise probability. Rank IC, funded NAV and Sharpe are not applicable. All data was already exposed. External requests: 0.




## Next decision




This is a negative result for this long specification, not for genuine activism, which a name rule cannot isolate. A filing-text study of stated intent would need new SEC requests. A short version is not available because the engine has no short accounting. This is the second consecutive no-pass Batch on the Claude line, so expert consultation comes before any further Batch.

da--us-da003-engaged-holder-short-check-.title: DA003 — Engaged holder short check
da--us-da003-engaged-holder-short-check-.content:
# DA003 — Engaged holder short check

**No pass. Stocks with a fund's initial 13D really do trail matched stocks, but they already trailed before the filing and do not fade by Q+4, so this is persistent selection rather than month-scale event alpha. The liquid short leg failed the frozen market-slope gate by 0.0015. This is conditional spread evidence on exposed development data, with no short ledger, and it is not Alpha.**




DA002 lost 6.04% a quarter buying fund-like initial 13D subjects. On 2026-11-03 the owner authorized short-sale research, so this round asked two questions. Was that loss real or an artifact of the benchmark? If it was real, could a short capture it? The round reused DA002's frozen events and seven windows (the rebuild matched DA002's event hash) and removed 7 names whose listed filer had been taken for the subject. External requests: 0.




## Results




| Gate | Rule | Observed | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 | Clean names rank below their cell median in Q+1 | 44.8th percentile, permutation p 0.004, 6 of 7 windows | yes |
| S2 | More bottom-5% hits than chance | 9.0% vs 5.4% null, p 0.015 (corrected) | yes |
| S3 | Inverted names, with no event in their own stock, do not lag | 49.9, p 0.49 | yes |
| S4 | Liquid short spread after 3%/yr borrow | +2.30% a quarter, 5 of 7 windows | yes |
| S5 | Liquid spread slope on the universe within ±0.25 | −0.2515 | **no** |
| S6 | Q+1 shortfall above Q+3 and Q+4 | 5.35 vs 4.66 points | yes |




The loss is not a benchmark artifact. Clean names collect more bad outcomes and fewer big winners (3.4% top-5% hits) than their cells, and the inverted names do not lag. It is not an event effect either. Two quarters before the filing, the same names already ranked at the 44.3rd percentile (p 0.018). In the filing quarter they ranked at 52.5. Through Q+4 the ranks run 44.7, 42.9, 46.5 and 44.1, so there is no month-scale fade. The fund-filer group does not clearly differ from the clean non-fund group, which ranks at 47.2.




The money sits in thin names: +4.49% a quarter, positive in 7 of 7 windows. Those small issuers with new 5% holders are where borrow is scarce and expensive, and the activation requires borrow evidence before any funded claim. The liquid leg returns +2.30% with a t of about 0.7, and every leave-one-window-out mean stays positive, from +0.62% to +4.66%. It depends on removing the inverted large financials, and it has only 71 names.




## Limits




- **Quarterly data.** Prices are quarter-end closes without dividends. Borrow is a proxy at 0.5% or 3% a year, and margin, recall and Rule 201 are not modelled.
- **Liquid tier.** It uses one day's dollar volume with no market-cap floor.
- **Pre-filing check.** It drops 28% of names and is biased upward, so it is a diagnostic only.
- **Negative control.** It holds 43 mostly large names, so it has little power.
- **Inversion flag.** It reads later indexes, a small identity look-ahead.
- **Post-result corrections.** Expert's audit found no defect that changes a gate. correction record records the S2 null and flag corrections.




Evidence: study plan, short-side check script, study results, tail and missing-data audit, expert response. Source revision for the run: 4930e70.

# DA004 — Confirmed fundamentals where price lagged (DAG001 round 2)

**No pass. Top-quintile confirmed-improvement names whose prior-quarter return was below the median earned +1.09% a quarter over matched stocks after costs, with no market link (slope -0.04). But they were positive in only 4 of 6 windows against the required 5, and the t-like ratio is 0.51. The names whose price had already risen were no weaker (+1.89%), so the data gives no evidence either way that lagging price marks the underreaction. This is a failed screen on exposed development data, not Alpha.**




DA001's broad top decile moved with the market. This round asked Expert's narrower question: if investors anchor on price trend, confirmed improvement should be underpriced where price has not yet acknowledged it, and it should beat stocks of the same liquidity and prior return. In matched cells L0 shows no market link, but H0 in the same cells keeps a slope of 0.46, so matching alone does not remove it. What remains for L0 is a small, unstable edge at the 51st percentile of the matched cell, and no difference by prior price can be shown.




## Results




| Measure | L0, prior below median | H0, prior at or above | Required of L0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1 pooled Q+1 within-cell percentile | 51.33 | 51.76 | above 50 |

| G2 windows positive | 4 of 6 | 3 of 6 | at least 5 |
| G3 slope on control-universe return | -0.04 | 0.46 | at most 0.25 |
| G4 Q+1 and Q+2 average over Q+3 and Q+4 (3 cohorts) | +1.19% vs -1.38% | +1.12% vs +1.73% | above |
| Verdict | G2 fails | G2, G3, G4 fail | all four |




| Formation | Control universe Q+1 | L0 names | L0 net matched excess | L0 percentile | H0 net matched excess |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-03-31 | +8.8% | 178 | +4.4% | 54.9 | +4.8% |
| 2025-06-30 | +8.9% | 132 | +0.5% | 50.7 | -0.7% |
| 2025-09-30 | +0.1% | 174 | -1.3% | 49.6 | +1.7% |
| 2025-12-31 | +0.3% | 154 | -6.9% | 40.6 | -4.3% |
| 2026-03-31 | +18.4% | 209 | +1.3% | 50.8 | +10.2% |
| 2026-06-30 | -5.2% | 167 | +8.5% | 60.3 | -0.3% |




## Diagnostics




The within-cell permutation p for L0 is 0.080, but it treats names as independent; window percentiles vary far more than that allows, and a window-clustered t on G1 is about 0.44. Dropping 2026-06-30 turns its mean to -0.40%. Doubled costs leave +0.44% in 3 of 6 windows, and charging -100% to names missing at the next snapshot leaves +0.65% in 3 of 6. L0 puts 7.0% of name-windows in the top 5% of its cells and 7.6% in the bottom 5%. In cells of about 30 controls a chance name reaches either tail about 6.5% of the time, so both rates are near chance, and the 5% null in study results overstates them. Liquid names (formation dollar volume of at least $20m) earned +2.00% in 4 of 6 windows, and thin names lost 1.66%.




L0's gross matched excess by horizon is +1.73% at Q+1 (6 cohorts), +2.41% at Q+2 (5), -0.60% at Q+3 (4) and -0.27% at Q+4 (3). Mean percentiles are 51.2, 51.1, 50.0 and 48.7. That is the right sign for a fade over months, but the later horizons rest on three or four cohorts. With DA002's coarser cells (dollar-volume decile by prior tercile), L0 is 51.73, +0.97% and 3 of 6. L0 minus H0 is -0.80% a quarter and positive in 2 of 6 windows.




## Method and limits




DA001's frozen signal table supplies the scored names and V0, the minimum of the within-formation ranks of year-over-year revenue, operating income and operating cash-flow changes over assets, all from one original 10-K or 10-Q. The DA001 panel was rebuilt with the false MPTI stock-dividend record removed (DA001 CORRECTION\_005). The rebuilt panel differs from DA001's only at MPTI's two affected entries. The top quintile was split at the scored median of split-adjusted prior-quarter return. Controls are the scored names outside the top quintile. Cells cross formation dollar-volume quintiles with prior-return deciles, both cut on the controls, and no cell was empty. Names and cells were frozen before any forward return was read.




Returns are quarter-end close proxies without dividends. Names missing at a later snapshot are held flat. Costs are a full round trip each quarter, at 25 bp per side above $20m of formation dollar volume and 50 bp below, with none on controls. Rank IC, funded NAV and Sharpe are not applicable to six quarterly marks of a conditional basket. The conditioning on prior return was proposed after DA001's results, so this is development reanalysis. A diagnostic binomial overflow was fixed before any output (correction record). External requests: 0.




## Next decision

da--us-da005-alpaca-history-coverage-rep.title: DA005 — Alpaca Basic history coverage for DAG001
da--us-da005-alpaca-history-coverage-rep.content:
# DA005 — Alpaca Basic history coverage for DAG001

**The free Alpaca Basic account can supply 2016-2024 prices but not a point-in-time identity, so DAG001 stays blocked on data. Daily bars start on 2016-01-04. All 12 delisted test names trade until their known final day. Raw bars move by the split factor across all six known splits. But bars are keyed by today's symbol. Renamed companies' history sits under the current ticker, reused tickers carry other securities, and the asset list has no CIK, CUSIP or dates. This is a feasibility check with no returns computed. It is not a performance Batch.**




DAG001's two no-pass rounds share six or seven exposed windows, and Expert asked for a longer history. A replication needs survivorship-free quarter-end closes from 2016 and a way to join each SEC filer to the right price series at each date. The prices pass that test. The join does not.




## Coverage




| Criterion | Result | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C1 history from 2016 | first bar 2016-01-04, AAPL and GE complete in the first week | yes |
| C2 delisted names trade to their end | LNKD 2016-12-07, MON 2018-06-06, RHT 2019-07-08, CELG 2019-11-20, XLNX 2022-02-11, CTXS 2022-09-29, TWTR 2022-10-27, ATVI 2023-10-12, SIVB 2023-03-09, FRC 2023-04-28, BBBY 2023-05-02, SHLD 2018-10-23 | yes, on traded bars |
| C3 renames continuous | no gap; FB, UTX, SYMC, NLOK and DWDP return nothing, and their history is under META, RTX, GEN and DD; YHOO and AABA keep separate symbols | yes |
| C4 raw bars unadjusted | pre/post close 3.87 (AAPL 4:1), 4.44 and 3.01 (TSLA 5:1, 3:1), 4.04 (NVDA 4:1), 19.61 (AMZN 20:1), 0.129 (GE 1:8) | yes |
| C5 dated identity route | asset list: 19,158 inactive and 14,395 active symbols, no CIK, CUSIP or dates, 12 of 28 test symbols absent; FSDS instance prefix equals the dated ticker for 77.6% (2025q1) and 73.8% (2025q4) of filers, against 90% required | no |




Two traps would bias a naive replication. After a name stops trading, Alpaca keeps emitting zero-volume bars at its last price: MON has 791 of them, running into 2022. Later, a reused symbol carries a different security: MON from 2021-03-16, and SHLD from 2020-11-06 and again from 2023-09-14, when it became an ETF. Marks must come only from traded bars, and a restart is a new security (correction record). History filed under the current ticker also mixes predecessors: DD's bars run back through the DowDuPont period, with the 2019 separation recorded as a reverse split, so its 2016-2019 bars belong to predecessor entities.




The corporate-actions endpoint helps with identity. One call returned dated name changes with CUSIPs (FB to META on 2022-06-09, UTX to RTX, NLOK to GEN), cash and stock mergers with effective dates, splits and spin-offs. The FSDS prefix misses are mostly a former ticker that the filer kept as its file prefix (REVV for RVTY, NCR for VYX, JEC for J). So the prefix, carried forward through dated name changes, is a plausible route to a dated map, but it has not reached 90% here.




## Power for the replication




DA004's L0 window net excess has a standard deviation of 5.2%. With about 35 quarter-end windows, a window-clustered t of 2 needs a mean near 1.8% a quarter. At a true +1.09%, the chance of reaching t 2 is about 22%. Expert's condition therefore applies: unless matching on sector or another control cuts that dispersion, even the full history is unlikely to settle DAG001.




## Method and limits




The study-local client sent only GET requests to three fixed paths on two Alpaca hosts, with no redirects or retries and 0.35 s pacing. It used 8 of 40 reserved attempts, all HTTP 200, 18.95 MB in total. Raw bytes are kept outside Git in the research cache and hashed in the request log. The 28 symbols and their events were fixed from memory before any request. The SIP feed was accepted on the Basic plan for these dates, which says nothing about intraday or recent data. No return, signal or rank was computed. Raw bars for these 28 symbols are now seen, which lightly exposes them for a later replication. The FSDS prefix test used cached 2025 files only, so its rate for 2016-2019 filers is unknown.




## Next decision




The owner chooses the identity route. The smallest request is about 37 quarterly SEC Financial Statement Data Sets files for 2015q4 to 2024q4, which are free and need no account, plus paginated Alpaca corporate actions for all symbols from 2016 to 2024, an estimated 20 to 60 calls. With those, a returns-blind map from each filer's instance prefix, carried through dated name changes, to a traded Alpaca series would be built and measured against the 90% bar. The paid Massive plan, which has dated ticker reference data, is the alternative and is not authorized. Only after the map qualifies would a frozen replication with sector-matched cells go to Expert, before any return is read.

da--us-da006-dated-symbol-map-report.title: DA006 — Dated filer-to-symbol map for DAG001
da--us-da006-dated-symbol-map-report.content:
# DA006 — Dated filer-to-symbol map for DAG001

**The map is accurate but incomplete, so the route does not yet qualify. On the seven cached quarter ends it names the right ticker for 88.1% of the listed universe on average, at least 84.1% in every window, against 90% and 85% required. When it names a listed ticker, that ticker is right 98.9% of the time. The shortfall is coverage: filings whose XBRL file name follows a filing agent's pattern rather than the ticker get no answer. That share is about 3% in 2016-2020 and rises to about 38% in late 2021. This is a feasibility check with no prices read. It is not a performance Batch.**




## Results




| Criterion | Result | Required | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C5 recall, R2 (prefix plus dated name changes) | mean 0.881, minimum 0.841 (2026-06-30) | 0.90 and 0.85 | no |
| C6 precision, R2 | 0.989 | 0.95 | yes |
| C7 historical prefix share, nonfinancial filers | 0.96-0.97 in 2016-2018; 0.619 at 2021-09-30 and 2021-12-31, 0.645 at 2022-06-30 | at least 0.658 (90% of 0.731 at 2024-09-30) | no |
| C8 acquisition | 33 of 33 SEC files verified; corporate actions complete in 10 pages | all | yes |




The prefix alone (R1) has recall 0.874 and precision 0.991, so chaining through Alpaca's 3,492 usable name changes adds only 0.7 points. In each gold window, 143 to 359 universe names have no ticker-form file name, and 115 to 150 get a wrong answer. Of the wrong answers, only 27 to 32 are another listed ticker. The rest are stale or invented mnemonics, such as LVIS for LEVI, ZIONS for ZION, WYN for TNL and TMB for CAG. Share-class roots also miss, for example GOOG for GOOGL and LILA for LILAK.




The historical pattern is the useful part. Before inline XBRL, almost every filer named its instance file by ticker. From 2019 onward, filing-agent names such as `` tm2412345 `` spread. So the map is strongest exactly where DAG001 needs new history, in 2016-2020, and weakest in 2021-2023.




## Method and limits




The 33 FSDS files for 2015q4 to 2023q4 (3.05 GB) came from SEC with the owner's stored user agent. Alpaca corporate actions for 2016-01-01 to 2026-11-03 came in 10 pages: 3,719 name changes, 2,068 cash mergers, 3,228 stock mergers and 252 stock-and-cash mergers. All 43 attempts returned HTTP 200, within a reservation of 98. Raw bytes are outside Git in the research cache. Only the SEC submissions table was read, and no price, return or signal was touched. The gold truth is Massive's dated mapping on the DA001 liquid universe, which covers 2024-2026 only, so 2016-2023 accuracy is inferred, not measured. The historical counts include unlisted filers.




## Next decision




This rule stops here, with no change after seeing the gold measure. The block is narrow and needs no new request: a filer with a non-ticker file name can borrow the ticker-form prefix of its own earlier filings. A follow-up rule that does this causally, using only filings accepted on or before the formation, is the next test. If that still fails, the remaining route is the paid Massive plan, which has dated ticker reference data.

da--us-da007-symbol-map-fallback-report.title: DA007 — Dated symbol map with a causal fallback
da--us-da007-symbol-map-fallback-report.content:
# DA007 — Dated symbol map with a causal fallback

**The dated filer-to-symbol map now qualifies as a development identity route for a 2016-2024 DAG001 replication. On the seven cached quarter ends it names the company's ticker for 91.7% of the listed universe on average, at least 87.3% in every window, with 99.3% precision. At least 91.6% of nonfinancial filers resolve at every quarter end from 2016 to 2024. No prices or returns were read, and no external request was made. This qualifies an input. It says nothing about the strategy.**




## Results




| Criterion | Result | Required | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C5 recall | mean 0.917, minimum 0.873 (2026-06-30) | 0.90 and 0.85 | yes |
| C6 precision | 0.993 | 0.95 | yes |
| C7 historical resolved share | lowest 0.916 (2024-09-30); yearly lows 0.973 (2016) to 0.982 (2020), 0.953 (2022), 0.925 (2023) | at least 0.824 | yes |




DA006's rule used only each filing's own file-name prefix. R3 adds a fallback: when a filing has a filing agent's file name, use the prefix of the same company's latest ticker-form filing accepted before the formation, then follow dated name changes. A ticker is also now correct when it is any share class of the same company. Against DA006, the unresolved count per gold window falls from 143-359 to 88-240.




The fallback is less accurate than a filing's own prefix. In the gold windows it adds 87 to 115 correct names but 18 to 26 wrong ones, a hit rate near 80%. It matters most in 2021-2022, where it supplies about 35% of resolutions (1,625 of 4,505 resolved filers at 2021-12-31). So the error rate in those years is probably higher than the gold measure shows.




## Limits




The rule was chosen after DA006's results on the same gold windows, so this is a development measure, not an independent one. Accuracy before 2024 is inferred from coverage. A replication should therefore treat a resolved symbol as confirmed only when it has traded bars at the formation and no other filer resolves to it. Historical counts include unlisted filers, which the replication's price and liquidity filters remove.




## Next decision




Per the frozen stop rule, the next step is a frozen 2016-2024 DAG001 replication plan with sector-matched cells, reviewed by Expert before any price is read. Quarter-end prices for about 35 formations would be new Alpaca requests and need the owner's approval.

da--us-da009-late-filer-cure-screen-repo.title: DA009 — Cured late filers, quarter-end screen (DAG004 round 1)
da--us-da009-late-filer-cure-screen-repo.content:
# DA009 — Cured late filers, quarter-end screen (DAG004 round 1)

**No pass, and the sign is the opposite of the premise. Names that filed an NT 10-K or NT 10-Q in the 92 days before a quarter end and then filed every late report lagged matched stocks by 11.9% a quarter after costs. The shortfall appeared in all 7 windows (t-like -4.3), and the names sat at the 40.4th percentile of their cells, with no market link (slope 0.03). The long premise, that the discount clears after the cure, is refuted on these windows. This is exposed development data, not Alpha.**




| Measure | C0 cured | U0 uncured | Required of C0 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Names per window | 16-35 | 1-11 | at least 15 (checked before returns) |
| G1 pooled Q+1 within-cell percentile | 40.39 | 49.30 | above 50 |
| G2 mean net matched Q+1 excess | -11.91% | -4.08% | above 0 |
| G2 windows positive | 0 of 7 | 3 of 7 | at least 5 |
| G3 slope on control return | 0.03 | 0.71 | at most 0.25 |
| G4 Q+1/Q+2 vs Q+3/Q+4, 4 cohorts | -10.1% vs -6.2% | +5.3% vs +6.9% | Q+1 above 0 and early above late |




The median cured name lagged its cell in every window, by 3.6% to 18.1%. So did the liquid tier, at 20 million USD or more of formation dollar volume (1 to 13 names). C0's gross matched excess was -11.0% at Q+1, -5.1% at Q+2, -8.0% at Q+3 and -2.0% at Q+4; its percentiles were 40.3, 46.6, 44.4 and 46.1. Doubled costs give -12.8%. A -100% bound on names missing at the next snapshot gives -16.2%. The permutation p for a percentile at or above the observed is 1.00.




**Method.** Events are NT 10-K and NT 10-Q rows in the cached EDGAR master indexes. A notice is cured when the matching 10-K, 10-KT or 10-Q is filed on or after the notice and by t-1.




**Universe.** DA002's rules, with point-in-time SIC to exclude blank checks: close at least $5, at least $100,000 of formation dollar volume, one security per CIK, and listed at least 270 days.




**Cells and returns.** Cells cross dollar-volume quintiles with prior-return deciles cut on the controls; 2024-12-31 uses dollar-volume quintiles only. Returns follow DA004: quarter-end close proxies and price returns. The event table was frozen before the plan and before any return was read. External requests: 0.




**Next decision.** The long specification stops here. The opposite side is DAG004's round 2 (DA010).

da--us-da010-late-filer-timing-report.content:
# DA010 — Timing and short side of cured late filers (DAG004 round 2)

**Promising development lead, not Alpha. DA009's cured late filers sat at the 46.4th percentile of their cells in the quarter ending before the notice window, at the 43.7th in the notice quarter and at the 40.4th after the cure. The shortfall therefore builds with the event rather than predating it, and T1 passes against the 45.19 floor. The liquid-tier short spread at 3%/yr borrow is +24.0% a quarter and positive in 7 of 7 windows, so T2 passes. Both rest on few names, on seven exposed windows, and on a direction chosen after DA009's result.**




| Measure | Result | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| T1 pre-notice pooled percentile | 46.42 (70 name-windows, 5 formations; permutation p for at or below 0.144) | at least 45.19 |
| Notice-quarter percentile (diagnostic) | 43.68 (106 name-windows, 6 formations; p 0.010) | — |
| T2 liquid short spread, 3%/yr borrow | +24.0% a quarter, 7 of 7 windows, 1-13 names a window | above 0 in at least 5 windows |
| C0 short spread at 0.5%, 3% and 20%/yr borrow | +11.8%, +11.2%, +6.9% a quarter; 7, 7 and 5 of 7 windows | diagnostic |
| Break-even borrow for C0 | about 48% a year | diagnostic |




Pre-notice percentiles by formation were 34.7, 46.3, 56.5, 44.3 and 47.7. That spread is wide, and 50 of 120 names were not in the universe two quarters earlier, mostly because they failed the price or liquidity floor then. So the timing evidence is weaker than its pass suggests: names that were already weak are underrepresented. After the cure, the shortfall narrows from 9.6 points below 50 at Q+1 to about 4 points by Q+4. That is a fade over months, but it is incomplete.




**Limits.** No short ledger, locate, recall, margin interest or payment in lieu of dividends is modelled. Late filers are often hard to borrow, and no historical borrow fee exists here. The liquid tier is a dollar-volume proxy without a market-cap floor, and one window has a single liquid name. External requests: 0.

da--us-da011-late-filer-short-replicatio.title: DA011 — Cured late filers, short side, 2016-2024 replication (DAG004 round 3)
da--us-da011-late-filer-short-replicatio.content:
# DA011 — Cured late filers, short side, 2016-2024 replication (DAG004 round 3)

**No pass. On unseen 2016-2024 history, cured late filers again rank below matched stocks, and the shortfall fades over months. But it was already there before the notice, and the borrowable names earn nothing.**




Cured late filers sat at the 45.3rd percentile of their cells (t 3.4). The short spread after costs and 3%/yr borrow was +4.4% a quarter, market-adjusted (t 3.0), and positive in 22 of 30 windows. The shortfall was larger at Q+1 and Q+2 than at Q+3 and Q+4 (t 3.3).




The two failures:




- **S5:** the same names already ranked at the 45.4th percentile in the quarter ending before the notice window, against a declared floor of 47.7.
- **S6:** the borrowable tier lost 0.9% a quarter.




On the readings declared before the data, the shortfall is persistent selection rather than a month-scale event effect, and a short of large, easy-to-borrow names would not have paid. This is not Alpha.




One data defect matters. A repair rule I added before events were joined turned SIGM's 2018 liquidating distribution into a 25:1 implied split, so the distribution was credited 25 times over, worth +2,455%. Without the fix, S2 and S4 also fail. The fix (correction record) was found by auditing the largest window outlier after results were read. Both versions are kept; S5 and S6 fail in both.




## Gates (after CORRECTION\_006)




| Gate | Result | Required | Pass | Before correction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| S1 rank | 45.31, window t 3.43, 25 of 30 windows below 50 | below 50, t ≥ 2 | yes | yes |
| S2 short spread, 3%/yr | intercept +4.37%/q, t 3.00; 22 of 30 positive | \> 0, t ≥ 2, ≥ 20 of 30 | yes | no (t 0.51) |
| S3 market slope | -0.08 | ±0.25 | yes | yes |
| S4 fade | early 4.60% vs late 2.18%, Newey-West t 3.26; month-1 share 0.31 | t ≥ 1.65, share \< 0.8 | yes | no |
| S5 pre-notice | 45.43 (712 name-windows, 55 dropped) | ≥ 47.65 | no | no |
| S6 borrowable tier T | -0.88%/q, 27 windows, 159 names | \> 0 | no | no |




Gross matched shortfall by horizon was 5.8%, 3.0%, 0.7% and 3.4% a quarter for Q+1 to Q+4. The notice-quarter percentile was 46.3. The robustness checks held their sign:




- excluding former SPACs: 47.2, +3.2%
- own-prefix names only: +3.7%
- -100% on control exits: +3.0%
- -100% on C0 exits: 44.3, +6.0%




The C0 spread was +4.8% at 0.5%/yr borrow, 0.0% at 20%/yr and -5.1% at 40%/yr, with break-even near 20%/yr. Late filers are usually hard to borrow, so the thin names cannot carry a funded claim. By sub-period the spread was +3.2% for 2016-2019 and +4.9% for 2020-2024. Leaving out any one year keeps it between +3.5% and +4.9%. Uncured filers (U0) were near the median at 49.3, with a spread of -3.8%.




## Method and limits




- **Data:** EDGAR master indexes for 2015Q3-2023Q4 (34 SEC requests), plus cached 2024. Alpaca Basic SIP raw daily bars and every corporate-action type for 2015-10 to 2024-12: 1,396 requests within the 2,100 reserved, eight chunks re-fetched without escrow codes (CORRECTION\_002).
- **Identity:** DA008's I2. At 2024-12-31 on Alpaca bars it had precision 0.997 and recall 0.903.
- **Split audit:** 393 implied splits, 11 cash-distribution moves kept as real, 79 records dropped, 1 re-dated, and 49 symbols (0.75%) unresolved, under the 1% line (CORRECTION\_003, CORRECTION\_006).
- **Shares:** from balance-sheet or weighted-average counts, because FSDS omits cover-page counts (CORRECTION\_004).
- **Coverage:** 30 of 34 quarter ends had at least 15 cured names (803 name-windows), so the sign threshold was 20.
- **Exits and distributions:** 206 spin-off distributions could not be priced and were valued at zero.
- **Not modelled:** short ledger, locate, recall, margin interest and payments in lieu.
- **Status of the data:** 2016-2024 is now exposed for DAG004.




## Next decision




This specification stops. On the declared readings, S1-S3 passing with S5 failing reads as `` dead `` for this line, a persistent shortfall rather than month-scale event alpha. The failed S6 separately says the tradable tier earns nothing. DAG004 goes to Expert for its judgment.

da--us-da012-profitability-crossing-scre.content:
# DA012 — First GAAP-profitability crossers above the index size floor (DAG005 round 1)

**No pass. Companies worth at least $1 billion that newly meet the S&P earnings rule earn nothing over matched stocks.** The rule requires positive trailing four-quarter and latest-quarter GAAP net income. After costs these names earned -0.35% a quarter against stocks of the same liquidity and prior return, at the 50.9th percentile of their cells (t 1.2), in 14 of 30 windows. There was no market link (slope -0.06) and no fade.




The predicted index-demand drift is absent at quarter-end entry on 2,275 name-windows from 2017 to 2024. The only gate passed is C5, and only because the placebo did worse: crossers worth $100 million to $1 billion lost 3.1% a quarter (intercept t -2.5). This is not Alpha.




| Gate | X0, cap ≥ $1B | Required | Pass |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1 percentile | 50.87, t 1.20 | above 50, t ≥ 2 | no |
| C2 market-adjusted net excess | intercept -0.16%/q, t -0.32; 14 of 30 positive | above 0, t ≥ 2, ≥ 20 | no |
| C3 slope | -0.06 | ±0.25 | yes |
| C4 fade | +0.12%, Newey-West t 0.23; month-1 share 1.10 | t ≥ 1.65, share \< 0.8 | no |
| C5 X0 minus B0 | +2.77%/q, t 2.07, 30 windows | above 0 | yes |




X0's gross matched excess by horizon was +0.31%, -1.48%, -0.07% and -1.11% for Q+1 to Q+4. B0's was -2.13%, +1.16%, -0.32% and -0.93%, at the 50.3rd percentile.




**Method.** Net income comes from FSDS: 10-Q quarters, plus Q4 derived as the 10-K annual figure minus three quarters. Each value is available from its filing's acceptance date. Eligibility is tested at each quarter end. A crosser is eligible now and known to have been ineligible one quarter earlier. 30 of 31 quarter ends from 2017-03-31 to 2024-09-30 had at least 15 X0 names (36 to 174). Market cap uses DA011's FSDS share counts. The universe, cells, return walker, corporate actions and costs are DA011's. The 2016-2024 price panel was already used for DAG004's cells, though no crossing return had been computed. External requests: 0.




**Limits.**




- A "first" crossing here means ineligible last quarter, so it includes repeat crossers. The 2018-06-30 window (174 names) reflects the reversal of the tax-reform Q4 2017 losses.
- The floor is a fixed $1 billion rather than the S&P index's changing threshold.
- Index membership is not cached, so inclusions themselves are not observed.
- Entry is at the quarter end after the crossing filing, up to three months late.




**Next decision.** This specification stops. The remaining question inside this Guess is timing: whether anticipating demand acts right after the crossing filing, before quarter-end entry.

# DAG005: index eligibility crossing

**Status:** dead. Expert, 2026-11-04. The mechanism failed where it could be tested at scale: 2,157 crossing filings above 1 billion USD earned +0.04% gross over 63 sessions (upper 95% bound near +1.6%) and -0.35%/q at quarter-end entry, with no dependence on the size floor. Scope: S&P GAAP-earnings crossers worth at least 1 billion USD, 2017-2024, quarter-end or post-filing entry. Excess above about 1.6% per 63 sessions is ruled out. First crossers (about 10 a year, 80 events) and non-member crossers are undetermined: too few, or index membership data is missing.




**Guess:** A company that newly meets the S&P GAAP earnings rule (positive trailing four-quarter and latest-quarter net income) while above the index size floor becomes eligible for index inclusion; rule-bound and anticipating buyers arrive over later rebalances, so its stock earns excess return that fades over months, while crossers below the floor do not.




## Simplified




We tested whether companies worth over $1 billion that first meet the S&P rule of positive GAAP earnings get bought up by index investors over the following months. Across 2017-2024 they did no better than similar stocks, whether bought at the next quarter end or the day after the filing, and smaller companies that cannot join the index did just as well. True first-time crossers are too rare (about 10 a year) to test separately. This closes the idea.




## Route




| Study | Reason | Variants | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DA012 | initial | 2 | First round: first GAAP-profitability crossers (trailing four-quarter and latest-quarter net income turning positive) with market cap of at least 1 billion USD, against dollar-volume and prior-return cells, quarter-end entry, 30 windows 2017-2024 on DA011's panel; crossers worth 100 million to 1 billion USD as placebo. |
| DA013 | returns | 2 | Second round: event-time entry at the first close after the crossing filing's acceptance, 63-session matched excess against same-cell controls over identical sessions, 2,157 X0 and 1,290 B0 filings 2017-2024. |

## Full Professional Report




## DAG005 — Index-eligibility crossing




**Closed `` dead `` by Expert on 2026-11-04.** The Guess held that a company crossing into eligibility while above the index size floor would draw rule-bound and anticipating buyers, and earn excess return that fades over months. Eligibility is the S&P GAAP earnings rule: positive trailing four-quarter and latest-quarter net income.




It did not. On 2017-2024 data, crossers worth at least $1 billion matched similar stocks whether bought at the next quarter end (-0.35% a quarter) or at the first close after the crossing filing (+0.04% gross over 63 sessions). Crossers below the floor did no worse.




True first-time crossers were the purest form of the idea. They number about 10 a year (80 events from 2017 to 2024 even with fundamentals back to 2012), too few to meet the declared test minimum, and they were never evaluated.

Reviewer: codex. Generated: 2026-11-04T21:45:15+00:00.

**The reported tests do not support month-scale, size-dependent excess return. The narrower first-crosser hypothesis remains untested.** I verified the supplied records and their manifest hashes; I could not reproduce the calculations.




- **DA012:** Across 30 windows and 2,275 X0 name-windows, mean long net excess was **−0.35%**, positive in 14 windows versus 20 required. X0 underperformed B0 by 0.93 percentage points; only E3 passed. The early-versus-late difference had t=1.28, below its gate. The negative month-one share reflects opposite-signed returns around a tiny denominator, providing little evidence of gradual decay. (Results)
- **DA014/DA015:** The freeze records report **88 X0 events across 22 quarters**, then **80 across 28**, against a minimum of 100 events across 20 quarters. | DA013 | `` returns `` | 2 | Event-time entry explicitly followed DA012’s null and month-one result: this counts as development. |

**Specified safeguards look reasonable:** acceptance-date availability, entry after acceptance, identical-session control returns, explicit costs, and freezes marked before return joins. Their implementation remains unverified. (DA012 plan, DA013 plan)




Material limits are:




- **Mechanism:** The fixed $1 billion cutoff and profitability rule are proxies. The packet does not establish dated index eligibility, exclude existing members, or document inclusion purchases. Repeat crossers further weaken the connection between the pooled tests and first eligibility.
- **Selection and dependence:** DA013 excludes 3,183 of 7,353 crossing filings through prior-quarter universe membership, plus entry and horizon exclusions.
